comment: Gate slice (issue 02) re-measure: coredoc-spec is 25,621 B after the standalone-acceptance commands and the artifact-path handoff, so its ceiling moves from 25,600 to 26,624 B; coredoc-workflows is 12,536 B after the stage-gate, skip-flag and parked-run rules, so its ceiling moves from 11,264 to 13,312 B. Both keep more than 512 B of headroom for issue 04's description sentence. Earlier OSS backport measurement: 5,809 catalog bytes across 23 skills after adding optional Jira and Git delivery. Router growth wires those capabilities and branch-start; implementation growth preserves existing intent guidance while adding branch-start. Body ceilings keep at least 512 B of headroom; these are bytes, not token estimates. Re-measure and justify increases; do not regenerate ceilings automatically. Issue 04 (gate sentences) re-measure: appending the mandated gate sentence to four descriptions moves coredoc-review to 344 B, coredoc-spec to 463 B, coredoc-implement to 503 B and coredoc-workflows to 547 B of catalog, and the catalog total from 5,809 to 6,613 B. The sentences are fixed wording and the pre-existing halves are all trigger phrases (the routed intents, the change kinds, the review surfaces), so nothing could be trimmed without losing a trigger: perSkillCatalogMaxBytes moves from 350 to 560 B and catalogMaxBytes from 6,100 to 6,700 B, leaving 13 B of per-skill and 87 B of catalog headroom. Body ceilings are unchanged and still hold (spec 25,863/26,624; workflows 12,945/13,312; implement 10,015/11,264; review 15,751/17,408). 2026-09-17: coredoc-spec's description no longer carries the gate sentence (it suppressed triggering: 0/9 fires on explicit spec prompts with it, 12/18 overall without), so the issue-04 four-description figures now describe three; every ceiling is unchanged.
